audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart on disk disagrees with the packet chart in six of seven rows, and — more damningly — it disagrees with the whys[] text printed directly beside it. Disk reads Skill / Tryndamere / Tryndamere / Skill / Skill / Tryndamere / Tryndamere.
audit.why: Row by row the prose already states the answer. whys[0] 'concede the window' = Tryndamere, but disk says Skill. whys[1] 'an even, cagey level' = Skill, disk says Tryndamere. whys[2] 'call it even' = Skill, disk says Tryndamere. whys[3] 'he edges the skirmish' = Tryndamere, disk says Skill. whys[4] and spikes[2] both call level 6 her premier window = Irelia, disk says Skill. whys[5] 'call it even' = Skill, disk says Tryndamere. whys[6] 'late game is his' = Tryndamere, which is the one row disk already has right. The packet chart matches the prose in all seven. The full and content layers currently agree with each other, so the fix has to move both together or the page renders two answers.
audit.corrected: Flipped six rows to the packet/prose reading, each as a matched full+content pair: [0] Tryndamere, [1] Skill, [2] Skill, [3] Tryndamere, [4] Irelia, [5] Skill, [6] unchanged. Proposed as one atomic group. Result is Tryndamere 3, Skill 3, Irelia 1 — consistent with 48.39% and a carry threat of 8.5/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every Tryndamere spike is named without a number, including Undying Rage, which the whole page tells you to track.
audit.why: Undying Rage is 120/100/80s for 5 seconds of unkillability, Spinning Slash 12/11/10/9/8s, Mocking Shout a flat 14s, Bloodlust a flat 12s. 'Wait it out, then trade' is unactionable until the reader knows the wait is up to 120 seconds and the escape is back every 12.
audit.corrected: Put the 12s Spinning Slash cycle in whys[3], the 12s Bloodlust cycle in early and spikes[0], and the 5s/120s Undying Rage figures in phases[4].why.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tryndamere.json Q, W, E, R cooldowns

audit.whatIsWrong: Irelia is credited with resistance shred in four fields — whys[4] 'max-stack passive shred', mid 'max-stack Ionian Fervor passive shred his armor and MR', spikes[2] 'shred his resists', wants.you[1] 'shred his resists'.
audit.why: Riot text for Ionian Fervor: 'When Irelia strikes enemies with spells she gains stacking bonus Attack Speed. At maximum stacks she also gains bonus damage on hit.' There is no armour or MR reduction anywhere in her kit. Against a champion who buys crit and Death's Dance rather than resistances, telling the reader a shred is carrying the fight sends them into an extended duel with the wrong expectation.
audit.corrected: Replaced all four with attack speed / max-stack bonus damage on hit.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mocking Shout is described three times as a flat slow on you — whys[3] 'Mocking Shout's slow', late 'Mocking Shout's slow keeps you from sticking', wants.foe[0] 'use Mocking Shout's slow on you to hold spacing'. It is conditional.
audit.why: Riot text: 'Tryndamere lets out an insulting cry, decreasing surrounding champions' Attack Damage. Enemies with their backs turned to Tryndamere also have their Move Speed reduced.' The AD cut is unconditional; the slow only lands if your back is turned. That is the single most actionable fact in this matchup and the page states the opposite of it: it is why you never turn to chase or to walk away, and why facing him costs you nothing.
audit.corrected: Stated the back-turned condition in whys[3], mid and wants.foe[0], and turned it into the instruction — face him.

audit.whatIsWrong: Vanguard's Edge is described in five fields as walling off, cutting off or blocking his Spinning Slash escape (whys[4], mid, spikes[2], wants.you[1], full phases[4].why and breakdown.late).
audit.why: Riot text: 'Afterwards the blades form a wall that will damage and slow enemies that walk through it.' Walking through it is what the wall is for — it damages and slows, it does not stop. The derived 'terrain' flag on her R reads 'creates terrain, blocks paths and dashes', which contradicts Riot's own description; per the file's own warning I trust the description. The practical advice barely changes but the expectation does: a reader who believes the wall traps him will position for a kill that escapes, instead of taxing the exit and stunning him on the near side.
audit.corrected: Reframed all six fields as damage-and-slow on the way through, with the stun landing on your side of the wall.
sources: champ-data/_kits/irelia.json R description vs terrain flag

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer never names Bloodlust or anti-heal, and spikes[0] and early both attribute his healing to his passive.
audit.why: Battle Fury generates Fury and crit chance; Bloodlust is the heal, consuming that Fury on a 12s cooldown. Attributing the heal to the passive makes it look unpreventable, when it is exactly what Grievous Wounds answers. The full layer already lists Executioner's Calling in report[8], so the two layers currently disagree about where his sustain comes from.
audit.corrected: Named Bloodlust and its 12s cooldown in early and spikes[0], and put Grievous Wounds into late.

audit.whatIsWrong: early calls Defiant Dance a 'block' you can waste.
audit.why: Riot text: 'She takes reduced physical damage during the charge.' It is a reduction across the charge, not a block of one hit — which matters because his crit autos are physical and arrive in a stream, so the charge is timed against his damage window rather than against a single spell.
audit.corrected: Reworded to a physical-damage cut in early.

edits.after: Mocking Shout only slows you if your back is turned, so face him - but his crit and fury ramp and Spinning Slash (12s) keeps him away.

edits.before: Tryndamere's fury-fed crit autos out-DPS your single Q before you have E, so don't sit in his crit window and trade raw at level 1 — last-hit with Q off the wave and respect that his passive heals a chunk of his fury bar back. At level 2 your W (Defiant Dance) damage reduction lets you eat one crit-spin and live, but don't pop it into his Spinning Slash timing or you waste the block on his reposition. Level 3 is your first real window: E-stun (Flawless Duet) into a Q dash-reset is the only trade that beats his sustained spin, and if you whiff the stun you just lose the auto war.
edits.after: Tryndamere's fury-fed crit autos out-DPS your single Q before you have E, so don't sit in his crit window and trade raw at level 1 — last-hit with Q off the wave and respect that Bloodlust (Q) spends his fury bar for a heal every 12s. At level 2 your W (Defiant Dance) cuts the physical damage of a crit-spin and lets you live it, but don't charge it into his Spinning Slash timing or you spend it on a reposition. Level 3 is your first real window: E-stun (Flawless Duet) into a Q dash-reset is the only trade that beats his sustained spin, and if you whiff the stun you just lose the auto war.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are dangerous — his crit chance and fury sustain ramp, and he'll Mocking Shout to slow your Q chase and Spinning Slash away, so don't burn resets running at a fleeing Tryndamere. Level 6 flips it: Vanguard's Edge is your premier window — drop the blade wall behind him to cut off his Spinning Slash escape, then E-stun him against it and let your max-stack Ionian Fervor passive shred his armor and MR while you Q-reset off any minion. That's the one moment he can't kite you, so make it count.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are dangerous — his crit chance and fury sustain ramp, and Mocking Shout slows you the moment you turn your back, so never chase a fleeing Tryndamere with your back to him. Level 6 flips it: Vanguard's Edge is your premier window — the blade wall damages and slows anything that walks through it, so his Spinning Slash exit costs him HP and speed. E-stun him on your side of it and let max-stack Ionian Fervor on-hit damage finish while you Q-reset off any minion. That's the one moment he can't kite you, so make it count.

edits.before: Late game he reclaims the duel: Undying Rage keeps him alive at 1 HP for 5 full seconds, so your combo lands clean and still doesn't kill, and then his crit autos shred you while Mocking Shout's slow keeps you from sticking for another E. Don't 1v1 him on a side lane once his crit items come online — your snowball burst can't out-DPS an unkillable spin-kiter. Group instead, use your R wall to peel and zone him off your carries, and close on objectives before his scaling fully eclipses your stronger mid-game.
edits.after: Late game he reclaims the duel: Undying Rage keeps him alive at 1 HP for 5 full seconds, so your combo lands clean and still doesn't kill, and Bloodlust heals the fury bar straight back unless Grievous Wounds is already on him. Don't 1v1 him on a side lane once his crit items come online — your burst can't out-DPS an unkillable spin-kiter. Group instead, use your R wall to slow him off your carries, and close on objectives before his scaling eclipses your stronger mid-game.

notes: No mirror audit exists for tryndamere__irelia yet, so nothing to reconcile against — but whoever takes that side must land the same chart: Tryndamere 3 / Skill 3 / Irelia 1, with Irelia owning level 6 and Tryndamere owning level 1, levels 4-5 and 2+ items. The chart flips are proposed as one atomic group of six matched full+content pairs. Brief header says games 1310 while the packet says 465; I used the packet's 48.39%. The Vanguard's Edge correction is the one Medium-confidence item: Riot's description says the wall damages and slows enemies that walk through it and says nothing about impassability, while the derived terrain flag claims it blocks dashes. I followed the description per the kit file's own instruction, and phrased every affected field so it is true either way — the exit costs him HP and speed, and the stun lands on your side of the wall.
